evidenceAudit.scope: Adults with suspected acute coronary syndrome (ACS) in the emergency department: ECG and high-sensitivity troponin pathways, reperfusion for STEMI/occlusion MI, and early NSTE-ACS management. Verified against the Australian ACS guideline 2025 (Heart Foundation/CSANZ), NICE NG185 and the Saudi Heart Association biomarker position statement (2022). ESC 2023 and ACC/AHA 2025 texts were not accessible (publisher block).
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.

v3: user-supplied unverified doses (acs-user-revision-2026-10-11-v1) replaced with FDA-label regimens for nitroglycerin, ticagrelor, clopidogrel, prasugrel and enoxaparin; contraindications added. UFH dose removed (not in sources reviewed).
unverifiedSections: Fondaparinux, UFH and tenecteplase ACS doses — local protocol
Saudi cardiogenic shock consensus not reviewed in detail

pathophysiology.summary: ACS is myocardial ischaemia from an acute reduction in coronary flow, usually after atherosclerotic plaque rupture or erosion with thrombosis. It includes acute myocardial infarction (troponin rise with ischaemia) and unstable angina. Complete occlusion (STEMI or other 'acute coronary occlusion MI', ACOMI) needs emergency reperfusion.
keyMechanisms: Plaque rupture/erosion exposes thrombogenic material → platelet aggregation and thrombus; partial occlusion gives NSTE-ACS, complete occlusion gives STEMI/ACOMI.
ACOMI includes ECG patterns beyond ST elevation: high lateral, posterior and right ventricular MI, De Winter T waves, and LBBB meeting modified Sgarbossa criteria (Australian 2025).
Myocardial necrosis releases troponin; high-sensitivity assays allow rule-in/rule-out within 1–2 h using assay-specific thresholds and deltas.
Complications: arrhythmia (VF/VT), heart failure, cardiogenic shock, mechanical complications.

symptoms: Central chest pain or pressure, may radiate to arm, jaw or back; at rest or prolonged.
Atypical presentations are common in older people, women and people with diabetes.
physicalSigns: Signs of heart failure or shock (crackles, hypotension, cold peripheries).
New murmur (mitral regurgitation, ventricular septal rupture).
redFlags: ST elevation or ACOMI equivalent on ECG → emergency reperfusion
Ongoing pain, haemodynamic or electrical instability, acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock (very high risk NSTE-ACS → invasive within 2 h)
Cardiac arrest — do not use level of consciousness to decide eligibility for angiography (NICE)
precipitants: Atherosclerotic risk factors: smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, family history.
Non-atherosclerotic causes such as spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Tearing pain to back, pulse/BP differential, widened mediastinum — CT aortogram before antithrombotics.
Pleuritic pain, hypoxaemia, risk factors; CTPA.
Positional pain, diffuse ST elevation, rub.

differentials.condition: Type 2 MI and non-ischaemic troponin rise
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Sepsis, tachyarrhythmia, anaemia, renal failure — troponin rise without plaque event.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Within 10 min of first clinical contact; repeat if symptoms persist, change or recur; right-sided/posterior leads if inconclusive
ruleIn.expectedFinding: ST elevation or ACOMI patterns; ST depression/T inversion in NSTE-ACS.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: STEMI/ACOMI → emergency reperfusion. Continuous monitoring and defibrillator availability if ongoing symptoms or new ischaemic changes.
ruleIn.normalValue: Normal sinus rhythm without ischaemic changes

ruleIn.testName: High-sensitivity troponin (hs-cTn) — 0/1 h or 0/2 h, or High-STEACS
ruleIn.modalityTarget: On arrival and repeat per pathway
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Above the sex-specific 99th percentile with a rise/fall (assay-specific deltas).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use the assay's own thresholds and the same assay for deltas. Low risk: discharge; intermediate with elevated troponin: inpatient investigation; intermediate without: outpatient testing within about 30 days.
ruleIn.normalValue: Below the assay-specific 99th percentile (e.g. hs-cTnT below 14 ng/L — SHA)

clinicalManagement.title: First 10 minutes
actions: ECG within 10 min; continuous monitoring and defibrillator if ongoing symptoms or ischaemic ECG.
Aspirin 300 mg orally (chewed or dissolved) unless contraindicated.
Oxygen only if SpO2 below 90%; keep SpO2 at 96% or lower if oxygen is given.
IV fentanyl or morphine boluses for chest pain if no contraindication.
Exclude aortic dissection when suspected before antithrombotics.

clinicalManagement.title: STEMI / ACOMI — reperfusion
actions: Primary PCI preferred if deliverable within 120 min of first medical contact (NICE: within 120 min of when fibrinolysis could have been given). PCI-capable centre: within 60 min of arrival; transfer: within 90 min of first hospital arrival.
Otherwise fibrinolysis within 30 min of first medical contact, with an antithrombin (UFH or enoxaparin). Age 70 or over: half-dose tenecteplase as part of a pharmaco-invasive strategy.
After fibrinolysis: ECG at 60–90 min — residual ST elevation → immediate angiography (do not repeat lysis); successful lysis → transfer to PCI centre, angiography within 2–24 h.
Primary PCI: DAPT with aspirin + ticagrelor or prasugrel (clopidogrel if these are contraindicated or on oral anticoagulation); UFH (or bivalirudin). No routine GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor.
Shock within 12 h → angiography ± PCI; no routine IABP or VA-ECMO.

clinicalManagement.title: NSTE-ACS
actions: Anticoagulate: UFH, enoxaparin or fondaparinux (NICE: fondaparinux if no high bleeding risk and not going for immediate angiography; UFH if creatinine above 265 µmol/L).
Very high risk (instability, ongoing pain, shock, heart failure, arrhythmia): immediate invasive strategy within 2 h.
High risk: early invasive within 24 h (Australian); NICE: consider angiography within 72 h if GRACE 6-month mortality above 3.0%.
DAPT: aspirin + ticagrelor or prasugrel if routine invasive (prasugrel only once anatomy known and PCI intended); selective invasive: ticagrelor or clopidogrel.
Lower risk: ischaemia testing guides need for angiography.

clinicalManagement.title: In-hospital and discharge
actions: DAPT 6–12 months (high ischaemic/low bleeding risk); then long-term P2Y12 inhibitor over aspirin (Australian).
On oral anticoagulation: OAC + aspirin + clopidogrel for 1–4 weeks, then stop aspirin (PPI with triple therapy).
High-intensity lipid lowering: LDL-C below 1.4 mmol/L and at least 50% reduction; beta-blocker if LV impairment; cardiac rehabilitation; vaccinations.

keyPoints: ECG within 10 min; look for ACOMI patterns, not just ST elevation.
Aspirin 300 mg; oxygen only if SpO2 below 90%.
Primary PCI within 120 min or lysis within 30 min.
hs-troponin 0/1 or 0/2 h pathway with assay-specific values.
NSTE-ACS: very high risk within 2 h, high risk within 24 h.
pitfalls: Missing posterior or high lateral occlusion MI.
Prasugrel before coronary anatomy in NSTE-ACS.

patientEducation: Medication adherence (DAPT); call for help with recurrent pain.
Smoking cessation, diet, exercise, cardiac rehabilitation.
lifestyleAndDiet: Not applicable in the acute phase.
dischargeCriteria: Low-risk pathway result with normal ECG and serial troponins below the 99th percentile; or completed in-hospital management.
On secondary prevention with cardiac rehabilitation referral.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Cardiology follow-up; cardiac rehabilitation; outpatient non-invasive testing within about 30 days for intermediate-risk patients with normal troponins; DAPT plan documented.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: PCI if within 120 min of first medical contact; otherwise lysis within 30 min
Early invasive within 24 h (Australian); NICE within 72 h if GRACE 6-month mortality above 3.0%
Only if SpO2 below 90%; keep SpO2 96% or lower

contraindications: Syndrome of asthma, rhinitis and nasal polyps

regimens.duration: Maximum 3 tablets in 15 min; if pain persists seek emergency care
adjustments: Avoid if hypotensive or right ventricular infarction suspected (clinical caution)

regimens.indication: ACS — P2Y12 inhibitor (with aspirin 75–100 mg daily maintenance)
regimens.frequency: Then 90 mg twice daily (first maintenance dose 6–12 h after load)
regimens.duration: First year; 60 mg twice daily thereafter
adjustments: Aspirin maintenance above 100 mg reduces effectiveness (label boxed warning)

medicationPlan.note: Aspirin 300 mg loading is from the Australian ACS guideline 2025. Nitroglycerin, ticagrelor, clopidogrel, prasugrel and enoxaparin doses and contraindications are from the US FDA prescribing information (DailyMed). Fondaparinux and unfractionated heparin ACS doses, and fibrinolytic doses, were not found in the sources reviewed (the fondaparinux US label has no ACS indication) — use the hospital ACS/STEMI protocol. Check SFDA registration, hospital formulary and actual availability; registration does not mean the drug is stocked.
